item.title: Pope Leo XIV presses on in Algeria after twin suicide bombings rock first day of visit
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived Tuesday in the Algerian city of Annaba to walk in the footsteps of St. Augustine, pressing ahead with his historic pilgrimage even as twin suicide bombings on the first day of his visit cast a shadow over the trip.

item.title: Italy suspends defense deal with Israel in reversal by Meloni
item.description:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced on Tuesday that her government has suspended the automatic renewal of its defense cooperation agreement with Israel, a move that came just hours after the deal was set to extend for another five years.

"In view of the current situation, the government has decided to suspend the automatic renewal of the defense agreement with Israel," Meloni said on the sidelines of an event in Verona, according to Italian news agency ANSA.

item.title: Pakistan pushes for new U.S.-Iran talks as port blockade enters second day
item.description: The United States military began enforcing a blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports on Monday, escalating a six-week-old conflict as diplomatic efforts to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz have so far failed. Vice President JD Vance, who led marathon negotiations with Iran in Islamabad over the weekend, defended the move as a direct response to what he called Iranian "economic terrorism."

item.title: Ships slip past US blockade of Iran despite CENTCOM's zero-breach claim
item.description:
U.S. Central Command declared Tuesday that no ships successfully breached its naval blockade of Iranian ports during the first 24 hours of enforcement, even as independent maritime data suggested several vessels slipped through the Strait of Hormuz unchallenged.

CENTCOM said in a post on X that more than 10,000 U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force personnel, over a dozen warships, and dozens of aircraft are deployed to enforce the blockade, which took effect at 1400 GMT on Monday. Six merchant vessels complied with orders to turn back toward Iranian ports in the Gulf of Oman, the command said. The blockade is being "enforced impartially against vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports and coastal areas," CENTCOM stated, while emphasizing that freedom of navigation remains in place for ships transiting to non-Iranian ports.

item.title: Saudi Arabia urges US to lift Hormuz blockade as standoff enters second day
item.description: Saudi Arabia is pressing the United States to pull back its naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz, warning that the escalation risks destabilizing the region and triggering Iranian retaliation, according to India Today reporting on Monday. The diplomatic push comes as the U.S. military's blockade entered its second day on Tuesday, with Washington and Tehran locked in a standoff over the world's most important oil chokepoint.

item.title: Oil dips as Iran war fuels historic shift to renewables
item.description:
The war in Iran, now in its seventh week, has disrupted roughly 20 percent of the world's oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz and sent energy prices to levels not seen since 2022 — but it has also intensified a global pivot toward renewable power that analysts say could reshape energy markets for decades.

Oil prices dipped below $100 a barrel on Tuesday as Iran's president signaled willingness to end the conflict, according to The New York Times, but remained roughly $35 higher than a year ago. The crisis, triggered by U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran beginning February 28, led to the effective closure of the strait and strikes on at least 23 oil and gas sites across the region.

item.title: US, Iran eye new peace talks as Hormuz blockade enforcement falters
item.description:
The United States and Iran are in discussions for a second round of face-to-face negotiations after weekend talks in Islamabad ended without a deal, even as a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports took effect Monday and tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz tested both sides' resolve.

A White House representative confirmed Tuesday that negotiations are entering a "potential second phase," though no official timeline has been established, CNBC reported. Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian teams could return to Islamabad as soon as Thursday, though the venue, timing, and delegation details remain undecided, with Geneva also under consideration. The ceasefire is set to expire next week, adding urgency to the diplomatic push.

item.title: New footage shows Artemis II capsule opening after Moon mission splashdown
item.description: Four days after splashing down in the Pacific Ocean, newly released footage is offering a closer look at the recovery of NASA's Artemis II crew following their 10-day journey around the Moon — the first crewed lunar mission in more than half a century.

item.title: Scientists find 6,000 km³ of hidden magma beneath Tuscany
item.description: Two studies published this month are reshaping scientists' understanding of what lies beneath some of the world's most geologically active regions, with one finding that Yellowstone's magma originates far shallower than long believed and another uncovering a vast hidden magma reservoir beneath the rolling hills of Tuscany.

item.title: Europe plans Hormuz shipping mission excluding U.S.
item.description:
European powers led by France and the United Kingdom are assembling a post-war coalition to secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz that would deliberately exclude the United States, Israel, and Iran as "belligerent" parties, according to The Wall Street Journal. French President Emmanuel Macron outlined the plan on Tuesday, calling for an international defensive operation built around nations not involved in the fighting, as the transatlantic rift over the war widens into a concrete institutional split.

The initiative, announced by both Macron and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer on X, envisions a conference "in the coming days" bringing together countries willing to contribute to what Macron described as "a peaceful multinational mission aimed at restoring freedom of navigation in the strait". "This strictly defensive mission, separate from the warring parties to the conflict, is intended to be deployed as soon as circumstances permit," Macron said. European diplomats have indicated that European vessels would not operate under American command.

item.title: Trump says US-Iran talks could resume in Pakistan within 48 hours
item.description:
President Donald Trump signaled on Tuesday that diplomatic negotiations with Iran could resume in Pakistan within the next 48 hours, reversing his dismissive tone from just days earlier when he said he did not care whether Tehran returned to the table.

In an interview with the New York Post, Trump told reporters stationed in Islamabad, "You should really remain there, as something might unfold in the next 48 hours, and our interest in visiting is increasing." He praised Pakistan's Army Chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, calling his handling of the negotiations "exceptional" and citing it as a key reason for returning to the Pakistani capital.

item.title: OECD warns fuel-tax relief risks repeating 2022 mistakes amid oil crisis
item.description: The ongoing war in the Middle East, which has disrupted roughly a fifth of global oil supply since Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in early March, is fueling a fierce debate over the world's dependence on fossil fuels — even as governments rush to cushion consumers from soaring energy costs.

item.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to direct negotiations after first talks in over 30 years
item.description: Israel and Lebanon on Tuesday agreed to begin direct peace negotiations following what the U.S. State Department called "productive discussions" at the first high-level meeting between the two governments in more than three decades. The agreement, reached after talks hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State Department in Washington, sets the stage for formal negotiations at "a mutually agreed time and venue," according to a department statement.

item.title: About 250 missing after Rohingya boat capsizes in Andaman Sea
item.description:
Around 250 people, including Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals, are feared missing after a Malaysia-bound trawler capsized in the Andaman Sea, the United Nations said on Tuesday in a joint statement by the UNHCR and the International Organization for Migration.

The vessel departed from Teknaf in southern Bangladesh around April 4 carrying an estimated 250 to 280 men, women, and children before sinking on approximately April 9 "due to heavy winds, rough seas, and overcrowding," according to the UNHCR. Only nine survivors have been found, raising fears that the rest perished at sea.

item.title: Iran restores limited internet for businesses after 46-day blackout
item.description:
Iran has begun restoring a sliver of internet connectivity to select businesses after a nationwide blackout that has now stretched past six weeks, in what observers describe as an attempt to stem mounting economic damage rather than a meaningful loosening of digital controls.

State-backed telecom firms are offering a "pro internet" package that companies can apply for through a formal identity verification process, according to digital rights group ASL19. Applicants must explain why they need connectivity and provide supporting documentation to receive access to online services outside Iran, ASL19 and fellow monitoring group Miaan Group said.

item.title: Pope Leo celebrates Mass at St. Augustine's basilica in Algeria
item.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass on Tuesday at the Basilica of St. Augustine in Annaba, Algeria, completing a deeply personal pilgrimage to the land where one of Christianity's most influential thinkers lived and died — and marking the first time a pope has ever set foot in the North African country.

item.title: Google rolls out Gemini Personal Intelligence globally, excluding Europe
item.description: Google on Monday began rolling out its Personal Intelligence feature for Gemini to users globally, extending the AI personalization tool beyond the United States for the first time since its debut in January. The expansion, which covers paid subscribers on AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra plans, notably excludes the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

item.title: Sperm whale clicks contain vowel-like sounds, new study finds
item.description: Sperm whales produce click patterns that contain vowel-like sounds strikingly similar to those found in human speech, according to new research published in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The study, led by UC Berkeley linguist Gašper Beguš and collaborators from Project CETI (Cetacean Translation Initiative), deepens what scientists know about one of the most complex communication systems in the animal kingdom.

item.title: Satellite study finds urban methane emissions far exceed official estimates
item.description: Methane emissions from cities around the world have climbed roughly 6 percent since 2019, far outpacing official government estimates, according to a study published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The findings, based on satellite observations of 92 major urban centers, suggest that cities collectively account for about 10 percent of all human-caused methane emissions — nearly four times the output of the oil and gas "ultra-emitters" that have drawn the bulk of regulatory attention.

item.title: IAEA chief warns North Korea rapidly expanding nuclear weapons capacity
item.description: North Korea has made a "very serious increase" in its nuclear weapons production capabilities, the head of the International Atomic Energy Agency said Wednesday during a visit to Seoul, confirming a rapid expansion of activity across the country's key nuclear complex and the likely addition of a new uranium enrichment facility.
